Service: SAP HTTP Interface - Port 80 (Generic Web Entry)
Description: Port 80 is the standard HTTP port and, in SAP environments, often serves as a public-facing entry point to underlying systems. While not exclusive to SAP, this port is commonly used to provide web access to SAP services through reverse proxies, Web Dispatchers, or directly bound ICM or Java stacks.
Deployment Context: This interface may represent SAP Web Dispatcher acting as a load balancer or reverse proxy, or direct exposure of the SAP Internet Communication Manager (ICM) or Message Server. It is frequently used to simplify access to internal services (e.g., ABAP WebGUI, Enterprise Portal) by providing a clean, low-numbered entry point, especially in DMZ or externally accessible setups.
Access Behavior: Port 80 typically responds with HTTP content, and if SAP services are present, may reveal headers or HTML content indicating the backend stack (ABAP, Java, dual-stack). It often forwards to higher-numbered SAP ports internally (e.g., 8000, 44300) or redirects to HTTPS versions of the same services. Exposed paths commonly include /sap/bc/, /irj/portal, and /nwa.
Functional Capabilities: This interface may expose various SAP services, including the SAP GUI for HTML (/sap/bc/gui/sap/its/webgui), the ICM info page (/sap/public/info), Enterprise Portal (/irj/portal), and NetWeaver Administrator (/nwa). Depending on deployment, it may support authentication via login forms, SSO mechanisms, or be used purely for redirect or proxy purposes.
Security Implications: When port 80 is open and accessible externally, it can act as an entry point for attackers to enumerate SAP services, discover login pages, or fingerprint internal stack components. Misconfigured Web Dispatchers or reverse proxies may leak internal paths or permit unintended access to backend services. Lack of HTTPS enforcement may also expose credentials or session cookies.
Detection Goals: This module will attempt to fingerprint SAP content over port 80 by analyzing headers and page content, detecting redirect chains to high ports (e.g., 443NN), and determining if SAP Web Dispatcher or ICM is in play. It will also probe common SAP endpoints to confirm stack presence.
Assessment Notes: If port 80 is open and leads to SAP-related content, the host may be externally exposing core services. This warrants close inspection of access control, authentication, and transport-layer security. Public access to login screens or internal service paths via port 80 may indicate an unnecessarily broad attack surface.
